Local alpha Sα is a zero-sum multinomial sample of the American metacommunity, E[S|J,m,θ]≈θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ=2J_M ν, set by local J, per-capita immigration m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ, by drift-immigration-speciation, not by species-specific competitive ability. The present equator-to-pole increase in Sα is therefore a neutral gradient in effective θ,m,J with latitude, i.e. larger regional pool/speciation and reduced dispersal limitation toward the equator.

The statement “potential to out-compete many natives” is operationally vacuous under neutrality. The European insect is just one more neutral lineage added to the New World metacommunity and, by assumption, present in the propagule rain at all 12 sites: Tena to Ottawa. Its local frequency is set by metacommunity relative abundance, drift and m, not by directional exclusion. With fixed local census size the invader can only replace individuals zero-sum.

To first order the invasion is θ→θ+Δθ, a uniform uplift of the regional pool. In absolute species numbers

Sα(lat,t→∞)≈Sα⁰(lat)+ΔSinv

with ΔSinv≈ the neutral occupancy of a ubiquitous species, essentially latitudinally unbiased. The whole Sα vs latitude curve is shifted up in parallel, intercept raised, and dSα/dlat≈dSα⁰/dlat>0 is conserved in absolute terms. The equator–pole difference in alpha is unchanged in absolute species numbers; there is no neutral mechanism for a superior competitor to preferentially remove natives at high-richness equatorial sites and flatten the tropical peak. That is the formal neutral null to the niche competition story.

Current disagreement is absolute vs proportional gradient. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 maintain slope preservation / parallel shift as the strict neutral prediction, noting that any homogenisation is drift/dispersal driven not competition driven. Colleagues 7,10 stress neutral homogenisation: a pan-American high-m super-tramp raises effective connectivity, lifts alpha proportionally most at species-poor high-latitude sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte, erodes β-diversity and in log/proportional terms the |dSα/dlat| declines and the gradient tends toward the metacommunity mean. Colleague 2 and 4/5 also note this second-order effect: the fixed additive ΔSinv is a larger fractional increase where S0 is low, so the log-gradient looks shallower even while the absolute slope is retained.

Unresolved is the ultimate mixing limit. In the idealised complete-mixing limit m→1 local assemblages converge to the metacommunity distribution and the latitude signal could be lost, but that is neutral drift/dispersal homogenisation, not niche competitive erosion. For the practical re-measurement horizon the consensus absolute statement is slope-preserving parallel uplift; the proportional flattening is a neutral homogenisation artefact, not a competition-driven loss of the equatorial peak.
reflection_text.3:
The question is about the latitudinal alpha-richness gradient for a trophic guild under Hubbell UNTB after a European insect becomes pan-American.

Core neutral premises repeatedly invoked:
* Species are ecologically equivalent; local community is zero-sum multinomial sampling of a metacommunity governed by drift, per-capita immigration m, local size J and fundamental biodiversity number θ=2J_M ν.
* Expected local richness E[S|J,m,θ]≈θ ln[1+J/θ]. The observed latitudinal increase in Sα is a neutral gradient in θ(lat), m(lat), J and dispersal limitation, not niche/competitive superiority.
* “Potential to out-compete many natives” has no mechanistic content in strict neutrality. The invader is just one more neutral lineage added to the American metacommunity, θ→θ+Δθ, with pan-American propagule rain.

Implication for the slope:
* Strict neutral accounting to first order: invasion adds, on average, the same ΔS≈1 species to every site that can receive immigrants. In absolute species numbers Sα(lat,t)≈Sα⁰(lat)+ΔS_inv, so dSα/dlat≈dSα⁰/dlat>0 is conserved. The whole Sα-latitude curve is shifted up in parallel, intercept raised, absolute equatorial-polar difference unchanged. That is the neutral null to a niche competition-driven flattening of the tropical peak.
* The zero-sum nature means any local gain is at expense of other guild members stochastically, latitudinally unbiased.

Disagreement / nuance:
* Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 stress slope preservation / parallel shift. The competition-driven erosion / flattening of the equatorial peak does not occur under neutrality. Any change is not competitive.
* Colleagues 7,10 argue for eventual neutral homogenisation: a pan-American high-m immigrant raises effective connectivity and reduces dispersal limitation most at high-latitude, low-alpha sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Merida. The fixed absolute addition is a larger fractional increase where Sα is low, so β-diversity is eroded and local Sα converge toward the regional mean. In proportional/log terms the gradient is attenuated and |dSα/dlat| declines, tending toward a flatter latitude-independent neutral alpha in the idealised complete-mixing limit. Both sides agree this is drift/dispersal homogenisation, not niche competitive exclusion.

Current synthesis:
Strict UNTB predicts no directional competitive loss of natives, so competition-driven erosion/flattening of the equatorial peak does not occur. To first order the latitudinal gradient is retained and the curve is shifted up roughly in parallel by the ubiquitous invader. A secondary neutral homogenisation effect makes the proportional gradient appear slightly shallower over very long timescales as effective m is raised and sites converge toward the metacommunity expectation; in the limit of complete mixing the latitude signal would disappear. Unresolved is whether the question’s “ultimately” calls for the short-term parallel-shift null or the long-run homogenisation limit toward a flatter slope, and how to weight additive absolute species-number accounting vs proportional/log accounting and zero-sum vs additive richness.
reflection_text.1:
The question is the fate of the latitudinal α-richness slope for a trophic guild after a pan-American European invader establishes at all 12 sites from Tena Ecuador to Ottawa Canada under Hubbell’s UNTB.

Core neutral commitments repeatedly invoked and now stable across rounds:
* Ecological equivalence, per-capita birth-death-speciation equal; “has the potential to out-compete many natives” is operationally vacuous under UNTB.
* Local community = zero-sum multinomial sample of a metacommunity: E[S|J,m,θ]≈θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ=2J_M ν, immigration m, local size J. The observed latitudinal α-gradient is the neutral gradient in effective θ,m,J with latitude, not a competitive gradient.
* Invader is one more neutral lineage. Its local frequency is set by metacommunity relative abundance, drift and site m, not by directional exclusion.

Consensus from round 1 public:
Absolute species numbers. To first order the invasion is θ→θ+Δθ and a ubiquitous immigrant. Sα(lat)≈Sα⁰(lat)+ΔS_inv with ΔS_inv ≈ same expected increment wherever the species can immigrate. Hence dSα/dlat≈dSα⁰/dlat>0 is conserved; the whole Sα-latitude curve shifts up in parallel, intercept rises, equatorial–polar difference in absolute species numbers is maintained. No neutral mechanism for systematic competitive loss of natives at the equator and no competition-driven flattening of the α-richness vs latitude relationship.

Disagreement / nuance:
Colleagues 10 and 7 argue the neutral homogenisation effect is more than a trivial parallel shift. A truly pan-American, high-m super-tramp raises effective connectivity and reduces dispersal limitation, and the reduction is non-uniform: high-latitude, low-α sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte were previously most dispersal limited relative to the speciation-rich equatorial portion of the metacommunity. In the zero-sum sampler a ubiquitous species inflates occupancy everywhere but the fractional/proportional impact is largest where α is lowest. Beta diversity is eroded, local assemblages converge toward the metacommunity distribution, and in proportional/log terms the equator-to-pole contrast is attenuated; |dSα/dlat| declines over time and in the idealised m→1 complete-mixing limit the latitude signal tends to a flat, latitude-independent neutral α. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 treat this as a second-order proportional homogenisation / sampling concave effect, not a change in the absolute slope, and state the neutral null as essentially slope-preserving parallel shift.

Current working position:
Under strict UNTB the competitive mechanism invoked by the researchers has no effect. In absolute species numbers the latitudinal α-gradient is maintained by drift-immigration-speciation and the slope dSα/dlat is essentially unchanged, with only a parallel upward intercept shift due to the ubiquitous invader. The proportional/log gradient can be described as mildly homogenised because a fixed additive species is a larger fractional increase at species-poor high-latitude sites; that is neutral drift-dispersal homogenisation, not niche competitive erosion of the tropical peak.

Unresolved: how to formally state the long-run neutral limit of complete mixing. Whether to frame it as an ultimate convergence to a flat latitude-independent α via neutral homogenisation, or as a conserved metacommunity-driven absolute slope with a conserved proportional gradient. The tension remains absolute vs proportional slope and whether homogenisation is a distinct neutral dispersal-drift effect beyond the parallel shift. The niche expectation of a competition-driven flattening of the equatorial peak is not realised under neutrality.

I think the first-order parallel shift that Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 are describing is the right neutral null for an infinitesimal addition, and it is important to keep ecological equivalence front and centre. Once the European lineage is in the New World propagule rain it is one more ecologically equivalent lineage, the 12 sites are zero-sum multinomial samples of one American guild metacommunity

E[S|J,m,θ]≈θ ln[1+J/θ], θ=2J_M ν

and with fixed J the invader can only replace individuals. To first order θ→θ+Δθ and Sα(lat)≈Sα⁰(lat)+ΔSinv is formally correct in absolute species numbers.

The revisit horizon the group is planning is not infinitesimal. A truly pan-American, highly mobile neutral lineage does two neutral things at once: it adds Δθ to the regional pool and it raises effective inter-site immigration and reduces dispersal limitation. The second effect is strongly site asymmetric.

m_eff increases much more proportionally at the previously most dispersal limited sites, Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, and to a lesser extent Merida, Belmopan, Managua, Yoro, than at Tena, Sarapiqui, Barro Colorado Island where m was already high and Sα is already close to the regional expectation set by high θ and low dispersal limitation. 

The sampling function is concave in θ:
dE/dθ = ln[1+J/θ] – J/(θ+J) decreasing in θ.
A uniform Δθ therefore gives diminishing absolute returns where θ is already large. Equatorial sites are the high-θ, high-m end of the neutral gradient and are saturating; temperate sites sit on the steeper part of θ ln[1+J/θ]. A fixed additive ΔSinv is therefore a much larger fractional increase where S0 is low.

That is neutral drift-immigration homogenisation, not niche competition. The 12 samples are being re-drawn from a larger, more homogenised metacommunity with a common high-m lineage in the rain everywhere. Local assemblages converge toward the metacommunity mean, β-diversity is eroded, and Sα,equator – Sα,pole is attenuated over the time scale of re-measurement.

In practice the biologically relevant latitudinal gradient researchers will fit is the proportional / log gradient and the empirical regression slope of alpha on latitude. The species-poor northern sites are pulled up toward the mean while the species-rich equatorial sites have little room to gain. The operational slope of alpha vs latitude therefore declines in magnitude, and in the neutral complete-mixing limit m→1 |dSα/dlat|→0.

This is pure neutral homogenisation under ecological equivalence. The absolute species number lift looks parallel for a moment, but ultimately the neutral prediction for the slope they will actually measure when they revisit Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui, Managua, Yoro, Belmopan, Merida, Miami, Charlotte, State College and Ottawa is a shallower, homogenised gradient.
